settings.sources: Points were read from published figures by pixel position against the figure grid lines, so each Cd carries about +-0.005 and each Reynolds number or spin ratio about +-2 %. They are wind-tunnel data, the fitting set for the flight-kernel drag law (#15443 F1); the launch-monitor rows in reference_shots_15443.json are the held-out test and must never be fitted.

choi_2006_dimpled_sphere_cd_vs_re.source: Choi, J., Jeon, W.-P. and Choi, H. (2006) Mechanism of drag reduction by dimples on a sphere. Physics of Fluids 18, 041702, doi:10.1063/1.2191848, Fig. 1 (dimpled sphere, filled diamonds). Non-spinning 150 mm sphere, 392 dimples, k/d = 0.004, stated to be dynamically similar to a production ball without rotation; the text gives a nearly constant Cd from Re 0.9e5.

bearman_harvey_1976_cd_vs_re.source: Bearman, P. W. and Harvey, J. K. (1976) Golf ball aerodynamics. Aeronautical Quarterly 27(2), 112-122, non-spinning ball as replotted in Choi et al. (2006) Fig. 1 (crosses); k/d = 0.009. Not fitted: deeper dimples than a production ball, crisis near Re 0.5e5 and a higher floor (Crabill, Witherden and Jameson 2018, arXiv:1806.00378, section 1).

bearman_harvey_1976_spin.source: Bearman and Harvey (1976) conventional ball, Cd and Cl against spin ratio S = omega r / U as replotted in Crabill et al. (2018) Fig. 6b (red Cd and blue Cl curves). The data end at S of about 0.28 to 0.29; nothing above that is measured.

lyu_2018_still_air.source: Lyu, Kensrud, Smith and Tosaya (2018) Aerodynamics of golf balls in still air. Proceedings 2(6), 238, doi:10.3390/proceedings2060238, abstract: 13 production balls, non-spinning Cd near 0.5 at Re 5e4 and close to 0.2 at Re 1e5. Held-out wind-tunnel-independent check, not fitted.
